summary: A fast, ten-minute hidden-role party game where everyone gets a secret role and character abilities happen once at night, then the whole group argues and votes on who's a werewolf. There's no elimination and no moderator needed, so it plays quickly and repeatedly with large mixed groups.
praised: extremely fast, easy to teach to newcomers
great for large groups and quick repeat plays
clever design lets anyone run it via the companion app with no dedicated moderator
criticised: outcome leans heavily on group bluffing skill and social dynamics rather than strategy
can feel like a coin-flip when players are quiet or new to bluffing
loses novelty after many plays with the same group

interaction.kind: hidden-role deduction, accusation, and a single group vote deciding everyone's fate
interaction.detail: The whole ten-minute game is players talking, lying, and pointing fingers at each other based on secret night actions, ending in one shared vote that can eliminate any player. There is no private board at all — the entire game state is the conversation and suspicion between players.
interaction.said: "you have to convince everyone else you're not the werewolf", accusation and bluffing are the entire game

scoring.how_you_win: After a single night of secret role abilities and a day of discussion, everyone votes simultaneously to lynch one player; the village team wins if a Werewolf is lynched, the Werewolf team wins if not, and a lone role like the Tanner wins instead if they are the one lynched.
